- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent forecasts.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and prices drop, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates prices during low-news periods (news volume = 0); adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for suppressed volatility.
- When sentiment change is negative and recent, model tends to lag; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment to catch early reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 3–5 consecutive price peaks; apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and news volume is high, model overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
